title: Urban Region Representation Learning: A Survey of Data, Methodological Families, Applications, and Evaluation
content: Urban computing increasingly relies on representations of bounded areas such as neighborhoods, census tracts, and traffic-analysis zones. Urban Region Representation Learning (URRL) transforms heterogeneous spatial-structural data, human mobility, POIs and urban text, urban imagery, and societal or environmental evidence into reusable region representations for functional inference, socioeconomic estimation, mobility and demand prediction, and emerging urban reasoning tasks. The URRL literature spans statistical context and spatial-smoothness modeling, graph-based relational learning, contrastive and self-supervised alignment, and foundation-model-based knowledge transfer and task adaptation. Although existing surveys provide valuable perspectives on urban data fusion and broad geospatial representation learning, they do not jointly examine the region as the learned unit, the hybrid composition of modern URRL systems, and the comparability of their evaluation protocols. To address this gap, we review URRL through an integrated data-method-application-evaluation framework. We examine how urban evidence is aggregated to regions and constrained by scale, vintage, coverage, and measurement bias. We then organize representative methods into four dominant, non-exclusive families and use inductive bias to interpret their representation mechanisms, learning signals, and imported knowledge. Finally, we synthesize applications and develop a protocol-aware evaluation framework that distinguishes resources, experimental configurations, and public benchmarks, while separating within-city reuse from geographic, partition, temporal, and missing-evidence generalization.
